Compare the fit and classification of mixture models

Source: R/compare-models.R
compare_models.Rd

compare_models() compares alternative mixture models fitted to the same observed data. It supports assessment of the number of latent classes and other model specifications by presenting evidence about model fit, complexity, classification, and convergence.

Information criteria summarise the trade-off between fit and the number of estimated parameters. Classification measures provide complementary information about the separation and relative size of the classes, while convergence summaries help identify estimation problems that may compromise the comparison. These measures address different aspects of a solution and should be interpreted together.

The function accepts separately fitted models or candidates from an enumeration grid and returns their comparison statistics in a single table. BIC differences express each model's distance from the smallest BIC among the candidates; normalised BIC weights summarise their relative support within that set. The function does not select a final model.

Usage

compare_models(
  ...,
  n_profiles = NULL,
  n_group_classes = NULL,
  cutoff = 0.8,
  test = c("none", "lrt")
)

Arguments

...

Either an enumeration grid from enumerate_classes() followed by the candidates to compare (none for all of them, or a selection through n_profiles and n_group_classes); or two or more fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate(); or two or more fits from mixture_regression() (with or without random). Named fits are labelled by their names, unnamed fits by their expression, and candidates by their candidate name. Labels must be distinct.

n_profiles, n_group_classes

With a grid, the class counts of the candidates to compare; NULL (the default) takes every count. Candidates whose fit failed are left out, with a message.

cutoff

For profile and class models, the average posterior probability below which a class is counted in avepp_below and group_avepp_below; a single number in (0, 1], default 0.8. Not used for mixture regressions.

test

"none" (the default) for the comparison table alone, or "lrt" to add a likelihood-ratio test of each profile, class or transition model against the one before it (see Details).

Value

A base data.frame of class latents_comparison, one row per model.

For mixture regressions the columns are model, n_classes, random, n_parameters, log_likelihood, aic, bic, sabic, icl, entropy, smallest_share, delta_bic, bic_weight and converged.

For profile and class models they are model, n_profiles, n_group_classes, structure (the covariance structure, NA without continuous indicators), n_parameters, log_likelihood, every information criterion of enumerate_classes()'s candidates table, profile_entropy, group_entropy, avepp_min, avepp_max, avepp_mean, avepp_below and the same four prefixed group_, smallest_share (the smallest estimated profile share, relative to all observation mass including any noise component), converged, n_best_replicated, and delta_bic and bic_weight, computed on bic_groups (the BIC that counts groups as the independent units; on a single-level model, the ordinary BIC). The values are those of the grid's candidates table.

With test = "lrt", three more columns: lr_statistic, lr_df and lr_p_value, NA in the first row.

Raises latents_bad_argument for fits that cannot be compared, for fewer than two models, for duplicate labels, for a group-class family grid (its own table, as.data.frame(grid), compares its candidates), for candidates named together with n_profiles or n_group_classes, and for n_profiles or n_group_classes without a grid; latents_unknown_candidate for a name, counts or selection not in the grid; latents_failed_candidate for a named candidate that could not be fitted; latents_incomparable_models for fits to different data. A cutoff outside (0, 1] fails the argument checks.

With test = "lrt": latents_bad_nesting for consecutive models that are not nested as described in Details, or that differ in their numbers of profiles or group classes; latents_reversed_likelihood when the more general model has the lower likelihood beyond the fits' tolerance; latents_no_converge for a fit that did not converge; latents_unsupported_weights, latents_unsupported_prior and latents_unsupported_noise for fits with sampling weights, a prior or a noise component; latents_bad_argument for mixture regressions. A fit with a variance at min_variance warns latents_boundary.

Details

delta_bic is the difference from the smallest BIC among the supplied candidates. bic_weight is the Schwarz weight exp(-delta_bic / 2), normalised across those candidates (Wagenmakers and Farrell, 2004). Incompatible data produce an error.

Candidates of an enumeration grid are selected by name, as the grid's candidate column shows them (compare_models(grid, "profiles3_groups4", "profiles3_groups5")), or by class counts (compare_models(grid, c(3, 4), c(3, 5)), where a single number means one group class). Alternatively, n_profiles and n_group_classes select candidates: compare_models(grid, n_profiles = 3) compares every candidate with 3 profiles, and compare_models(grid) compares them all. Latent class grids work the same way, with classes in the names, and the n_profiles column counting classes. Fits from multilpa(), lpa(), lca(), lta() or get_candidate() can also be passed directly.

With test = "lrt", each model is tested against the model in the row before it, as stats::anova() does: lr_statistic is twice the difference in their log likelihoods, lr_df the difference in their numbers of free parameters, and lr_p_value its upper chi-square tail (Wilks, 1938). List the models from the most restricted to the most general. A model is nested in the next when the two have the same indicators, coding, estimation settings and numbers of profiles and group classes, and the first only restricts the second: a covariance structure restricted letter by letter (EEI within VVI or EEE, and both within VVV), covariances of chosen pairs (local_dependence) within more pairs or a full covariance, fewer joint item pairs, direct effects or membership covariates, profile slopes shared across group classes, count dispersions shared across profiles; and for lta(), measurement invariant within measurement by occasion, homogeneous within occasion-specific transitions, first within second order, and fewer transition or initial covariates. These restrictions hold parameters at interior values, where the chi-square reference applies. A different number of profiles or group classes, or a stayer class, puts the null on the boundary of the parameter space, where it does not: those comparisons are refused and belong to bootstrap_lrt() or get_results(grid, "lmr").

Interpretation

Models must use the same outcomes or indicators and observational units, and their likelihoods must be comparable. Lower information criteria favour a model relative to the alternatives considered, but do not establish adequate fit or substantive validity. Classification separation should inform interpretation rather than serve as the sole basis for choosing the number of classes. Final selection also requires examination of estimation stability, model assumptions, and the meaning of the resulting classes.

References

Wilks, S. S. (1938). The large-sample distribution of the likelihood ratio for testing composite hypotheses. The Annals of Mathematical Statistics, 9(1), 60–62.

Wagenmakers, E.-J., & Farrell, S. (2004). AIC model selection using Akaike weights. Psychonomic Bulletin & Review, 11, 192–196.

Examples

# Compare trajectory and random-intercept growth models for 60 students.
few_students <- subset(growth_scores, student <= 60)
trajectories <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                                   id = "student", class_level = "group",
                                   seed = 1)
growth <- mixture_regression(score ~ wave, few_students, n_classes = 2,
                             id = "student", class_level = "group",
                             random = "intercept", n_starts = 3, seed = 1)
compare_models(trajectories = trajectories, growth = growth)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model         Classes  Random     k    LogLik      BIC    ΔBIC  Weight  Entropy
#> ------------  -------  ---------  -  --------  -------  ------  ------  -------
#> trajectories        2  none       7  -1277.94  2584.53  196.11   0.000     0.94
#> growth              2  intercept  9  -1175.79  2388.43    0.00   1.000     0.97

# Candidates of an enumeration grid, by name, by class counts, or selected
grid <- enumerate_classes(subset(course_engagement, student <= 30),
                          c("browse", "lectures"), "student",
                          n_profiles = 2:3, n_group_classes = 1:2,
                          model = "VVI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
compare_models(grid, "profiles2_groups2", "profiles3_groups2")
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1097.18  2231.78   0.00   0.996  2450.46     0.67       0.90      0           0.97             0.99
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1092.40  2242.62  10.84   0.004  2578.50     0.68       0.70      1           0.96             0.99
compare_models(grid, c(2, 2), c(3, 2))
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1097.18  2231.78   0.00   0.996  2450.46     0.67       0.90      0           0.97             0.99
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1092.40  2242.62  10.84   0.004  2578.50     0.68       0.70      1           0.96             0.99
compare_models(grid, n_group_classes = 2)
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model              Profiles  Group classes   k    LogLik      BIC   ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8  Group entropy  Group min AvePP
#> -----------------  --------  -------------  --  --------  -------  -----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -------------  ---------------
#> profiles2_groups2         2              2  11  -1097.18  2231.78   0.00   0.996  2450.46     0.67       0.90      0           0.97             0.99
#> profiles3_groups2         3              2  17  -1092.40  2242.62  10.84   0.004  2578.50     0.68       0.70      1           0.96             0.99

# Is a covariance structure that varies by profile needed? A
# likelihood-ratio test of each structure against the one before it.
shared <- lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"), n_profiles = 2,
              model = "EEI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
varying <- lpa(faithful, c("eruptions", "waiting"), n_profiles = 2,
               model = "VVI", n_starts = 2, seed = 1)
compare_models(shared = shared, varying = varying, test = "lrt")
#> Model comparison
#> 
#> Model    Profiles  k    LogLik      BIC  ΔBIC  Weight      ICL  Entropy  Min AvePP  < 0.8     LR  df      p
#> -------  --------  -  --------  -------  ----  ------  -------  -------  ---------  -----  -----  --  -----
#> shared          2  7  -1157.68  2354.60  8.54   0.014  2357.27     0.99       1.00      0                  
#> varying         2  9  -1147.81  2346.06  0.00   0.986  2346.52     1.00       1.00      0  19.75   2  <.001
